text: On a damp Thursday in Veyr, engineers for the Dunmarrow Waterway Authority confirmed that the planned canal tunnel beneath the Briar Ridge will stretch 11 kilometres, making it the longest single cut-through in the county’s inland transport scheme. The figure was released after months of surveying, following a winter in which bore samples and groundwater maps were quietly circulated among contractors. The tunnel, first proposed in 2019 as part of the old marsh route revival, is intended to spare barges a nine-mile detour around unstable embankments. Authority chair Elsin Marr said excavation could begin by late spring, pending permits. For many in Dunmarrow, the project carries the same patient ambition that once built the northern locks a generation ago.
